Alex / Mateo / Lauren — I ran a short-profile based on the telemetry and a set of conservative assumptions. Key findings and recommendations below (high level first, details + numbers in attached csv):

Summary recommendation:
- Baseline: Hybrid pool = 60% A100 (40GB) slots + 30% H100 (80GB) slots + 10% L4 (40GB) for low-cost short-request burst.
- Rationale: A100 (40GB) gives best predictable throughput for mixed-length workloads without over-indexing on long-context memory. H100 (80GB) reserved for sustained long-context queries and heavy KV-cache residency. L4 is a cost-effective low-latency worker for short-context/embedding-only routes.

Memory vs throughput tradeoffs (short):
- H100 (80GB): highest single-GPU effective sequence length before cross-device split; best for 8k-32k token sessions with large KV cache, but higher $/slot.
- A100 (40GB): strong throughput for mixed queries; good batching density; less headroom for very long contexts — will require request chopping or OOM fallthrough above ~10k depending on model + prompts.
- L4 (40GB ML-specialized): optimized for small-context low-latency; excellent cost per request on embed-only or small chat; poor for long-context generation due to model footprint and perf characteristics.

Throughput numbers (single-GPU approximations, batch mechanics):
- A100 40GB: 450–800 tokens/sec (dependent on model variant and quantization), can sustain ~1800 short requests/min when batching aggressively on 2–4 token generations.
- H100 80GB: 380–700 tokens/sec for long-context heavy pipelines, but supports larger KV caches and fewer cross-device shuffles. Good for 10k+ tokens session residency.
- L4 40GB: 1200–2200 tokens/sec on short contexts and small models; ideal for retrieval/embedding endpoints.

Operational recommendations:
- Reserve enough H100 slots to cover 95th percentile of long-context concurrent sessions; use A100 pool to absorb mixed load; configure L4 pool as cheap bursters and for embedding routes.
- Enable prefix KV caching (per-patient) with eviction policy tuned to session frequency; this reduces effective token work on long-context re-reads by up to 40% in our tests.
- Quantization: for A100 we recommend FP16 or 4-bit mixed quant for cost savings; H100 can take advantage of direct tensor core kernels for larger models without as much perf hit.

Attachments: gpu-sizing-matrix.csv (detailed slot counts and sim results), benchmark-screenshots.png (tail latency plots)

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk the table.

—Dev (Infra/Perf)

Alex — thanks for the details and thanks Dev & Mateo for the sizing work. Quick commercial framing to unblock Procurement: 

Proposed commercial structure (high-level):
- Pilot (30 days): 8 A100 slots + 4 H100 slots + 2 L4 slots (burst pool). This matches a conservative start for your current traffic and will allow us to validate tail-latency assumptions.
- Production reserve (12 months): scale to 48 A100 slots + 12 H100 slots + 8 L4 slots (committed monthly). We will provide a 12% discount on committed units vs on-demand.
- Fallback policy: Redwood-managed spill to A100 on burst; region fallback to us-east-1 where we have spare A100 capacity. H100 will be prioritized for pinned long-context lanes.

Next steps:
1) Confirm pilot start date and region (we recommend us-west-2 for proximity).
2) I will provision an initial SOW + MOP draft and pricing band for Procurement to review.
3) If procurement needs proof-of-work, we can provide a 7-day performance pilot with metric SLAs (latency and throughput).

CC-ing Mateo & Dev — if you both sign off on the slot counts in the csv, I'll put together the SOW and draft pricing today.
